key_insight: LLMs can recognize updated medical guidance without fully incorporating it into recommendations: the primary model showed a 32.3-percentage-point gap.
clinical_relevance: Providing updated guideline evidence may not prevent LLMs from retaining outdated recommendations, raising reliability concerns for clinical use.
method: Introduced ChronoEvo: 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 types of medical knowledge change.
Evaluated recognition versus incorporation across 14 models, with two-clinician adjudication of 300 responses.
Tested a revision-salience intervention to emphasize updated guidance.
evidence_signal: The primary model recognized 90.8% of revisions but fully incorporated 58.5%; clinician-adjudicated validation found a 40.3-percentage-point recognition–incorporation gap.
watch_item: Emphasizing revisions reduced outdated-content retention and improved clinical correctness, but did not significantly improve full incorporation.
paper_title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
